title.narrative: Output 8.1. Increased capacity of member States to develop new or reformed sustainable national social protection strategies, policies or legal frameworks to extend coverage and enhance benefit adequacy

description.narrative:
(1) On 9 September 2021, the Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa adopted the amended KP Employees Social Security Act 2021, which extends coverage of social security to ‘Construction Workers' (both in public-funded projects and private projects), and to workers earning 60% higher than the prescribed Minimum Wage in the Province. (2) A Universal Health Care (UHC) programme launched in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province achieving coverage of 100% of the households in December 2020. In 2021, UHC is being replicated in Punjab Province, which will be followed by Baluchistan province in 2022. (1) In 2020-21, ILO strongly advocated for expanded coverage through ‘Social Security Coordination Forum'. ILO undertook a study on the feasibility of extending social security to Construction Workers (under the German-funded Baldia Project). During 2018-19, the ILO Baldia Project and the South-South facility facilitated exposure visits for Social Security Institutions to Malaysia, including SOCSO, to study how informal economy workers were covered by social security. (2) ILO has undertaken strong advocacy for Universal Social Protection since 2016-including through a national conference in November 2020. ILO undertook a technical actuarial study for the first phase of the Social Health Programme in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province(KP) in 2018-19 and was requested a similar study in 2021 for expanding this programme to Punjab.
(3) ILO is providing strong support to Governments of KP, Punjab and Pakistan Administered Kashmir(PAK) in developing draft Social Protection Policies to align with aspirations of Employers and Workers in-line with international standards C102 and R202. In KP, ILO is updating a 2014 Draft SP Policy. In Punjab, technical inputs are provided and participation of employers and workers organizations is supported in policy dialogue. In PAK, various seminars were facilitated (jointly organized with other UN Agencies including UNDP and UNICEF).

description.narrative:
1) The Government of Pakistan established the first tripartite ‘Social Security Coordination Forum (SSCF)' in November 2020. The Forum has held three (3) meetings. This is the first time that a coordinated response has supported a number of positive initiatives to extend coverage, enhance comprehensiveness, and increase adequacy of benefits. These initiatives include joint coverage-campaign and awareness raising by the Employees Old-Age Benefits Institution (EOBI), the Employees Social Security Institutions-(ESSI) and the Workers Welfare Fund (WWF), study on extending social security to workers after their retirement; and three studies on covering informal economy workers.
(2)The Sindh Employees Social Security Institution (SESSI) has adopted and is implementing a modern digital information management system since August 2021 for an effective cash transfer system for disbursing pension to victims of M/s Ali Enterprise factory fire. (1) The ILO provided support to the SSCF by drafting and developing its TORs and composition of the Forum, proposing the preliminary agenda of meetings, providing secretarial support, and supporting the technical capacity development of SSCF members.
(2)The ILO is providing support to Sindh Employees Social Security Institution (SESSI) for upgrading the cash transfer system and its Information management system – under the German-funded technical support project.

description.narrative: The Government of Pakistan adopted the Mazdoor Ka EHSAAS (MKE) programme in March 2021. It was formally launched on 1 May 2021 and notified to the MKE Implementation Unit in September 2021. The 'Mazdoor Ka EHSAAS (compassion for Labour)' programme, which was jointly developed by tripartite stakeholders, englobes eleven (11) priority actions to promote social protection for informal economy workers and their formalization. A tripartite Labour Welfare and Social Protection Expert Group (LEG) was established to develop the Mazdoor Ka EHSAAS (MKE). The MKE programme will mainly support 27.3 million Informal Economy workers in the non-agricultural sector and 23.8 million workers in the Agriculture sector. The ILO facilitated a number of online and face-to-face meetings with participation of Government, Employers and Workers in the Labour Expert Group to develop the Mazdoor-ka-Ehsaas (MKE) programme. ILO also facilitated discussions in the meetings, providing necessary statistics and data, and collaborated with the EHSAAS Delivery Unit within the Government of Pakistan, Ministry of Poverty Alleviation & Social Safety Division, to launch the MKE.
